messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: HIGH - NovaCorp (enterprise, VPC) experiencing regional errors in us-east-1. Symptoms: 502s and increased latency for inference. Runbook: https://runbooks/internal/nova-failover. Pager: @Anna (oncall) @Mike R. @Jess K.
Anna (oncall): I'm on it. Acknowledge. Starting triage — grabbing logs and metrics.
Mike R.: spotting GPU node scale set flapping in us-east pool. Kernel OOMs on 3/8 nodes -> scheduler evicting pods. Might be underlying host issue, not model code.
Jess K.: Confirmed error spike on infra dashboards — token pipeline latency up from ~45ms to ~680-900ms for NovaCorp’s traffic, error rate ~18%. Alerts triggered.
Lee S.: I’ve opened a customer-facing update to NovaCorp (sent on their SLA channel). Told them we’re investigating and may fail traffic to fallback region.
Natalie P.: We have a warm dedicated pool in us-west-2 for NovaCorp (reserved). Capacity looks healthy and prewarmed with model variants. We can shift traffic there with DNS weight or routing layer.
Ryan N.: Networking note — their DNS is Route53 with health-check failover. Current TTL is 300s. For a smooth cutover we should lower TTL to 30, change weights to shift 80% to us-west then drain.
Anna (oncall): Agreed. Plan: 1) lower DNS TTL -> 30. 2) push 80% weight to us-west 3) monitor errors/latency for 10min 4) move remaining traffic and decommission connections in us-east. Keep NovaCorp in the loop. Who can make the DNS change?
Ryan N.: I can. Will push via CLI. Command I’ll run:

```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z111EXAMPLE --change-batch '{\n  "Comment": "temp lower TTL & weighted failover for NovaCorp",\n  "Changes": [\n    {\n      "Action": "UPSERT",\n      "ResourceRecordSet": {\n        "Name": "api.novacorp.internal.redwood",\n        "Type": "A",\n        "SetIdentifier": "us-west-2-primary",\n        "Weight": 80,\n        "TTL": 30,\n        "ResourceRecords": [{"Value": "34.201.11.22"}]\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}'
```

Ryan N.: I’ll also create a matching health-check for the us-west endpoint and run smoke tests after update.
Sean O.: Pre-warming note: we need to ensure model cache (KV) warmup on the us-west side for NovaCorp keys. Natalie, can you trigger a synthetic workload to populate caches?
Natalie P.: On it. I'll run a scripted warmup that hits the same prompt shapes NovaCorp uses. ETA ~4 mins.
Anna (oncall): I'll compose a short customer update to NovaCorp: "We are failing traffic to a standby region to mitigate increased errors. Expect brief 502s while clients re-resolve DNS." Lee, please approve.
Lee S.: Approved. Send at fixed cadence: immediate + 15m + 1h.
Mike R.: Root cause hypothesis: host kernel memory leak tied to an older CUDA driver rolling on that AZ. We've got crash logs. Dropping an excerpt:

```
[2026-02-28T14:03:12Z] node-az1-gpu-07 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 4522 (llm-server) total-vm:12345678kB, anon-rss:9876543kB
[2026-02-28T14:03:12Z] node-az1-gpu-08 kernel: oom_reaper: reaped process 4522
```

Mike R.: We'll mark the affected hosts for maintenance and cordon them post-cutover.
Jess K.: Running metrics now — after Ryan's TTL update (in progress). Watching error rate and route failovers.
Ryan N.: DNS change propagated. Route53 shows weight 80->us-west. Running curl probes against api.novacorp.internal.redwood (EDNS) to confirm.
Ryan N.: curl probe results:

```
> curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://api.novacorp.internal.redwood/health
200 0.122
200 0.118
200 0.130
```

Anna (oncall): Excellent. Natalie, how's cache warmup?
Natalie P.: Warmup complete. Logs show model KV hit-rate on us-west >95% for NovaCorp test keys.
Sean O.: Gradually shifting remaining 20% now and beginning connection drain in us-east. Draining strategy: set kube-svc traffic-weight to 0 and remove endpoints after 120s.
Anna (oncall): Monitoring in realtime. Error rate has dropped from 18% -> 1.5% in the last 6 minutes. Latency back to ~50-80ms.
Lee S.: Customer update sent: "We have shifted traffic to our standby region; service restored. Engineering is performing host-level maintenance in us-east; we will follow up with RCA." 
NovaCorp Support: Thanks for the quick action. Can you confirm if any data loss or request replays were involved?
Mike R.: No request payloads were dropped at the application layer. Some in-flight requests returned 502 during the flapping; we're reviewing logs for retries. No persistent state is written on inference calls.
Anna (oncall): Good. Next steps: 1) keep traffic in us-west until node maintenance done. 2) run full host soak and driver rollback in us-east. 3) prepare controlled return plan with staged traffic (25/50/75/100). I'll create the follow-up incident ticket for RCA and postmortem.
Jess K.: I'll capture alert noise and adjust thresholds to reduce noisy paging for partial AZ issues.
Ryan N.: Reverting TTL back to 300 only after final cutover and verification. I'll queue that change for later.
Sean O.: Handoff: I need to take night shift on this one. Anna, handoff note:\n- current state: all traffic in us-west, latency stable, error rate <2%\n- customer notified\n- maintenance plan: kernel/drivers rollback + soak in us-east\n- rollback plan: staged DNS weights if tests pass

Anna (oncall): Thanks Sean. I'm handing off pager. If anything degrades call me and Mike.
Sean O.: Acknowledge. I'll update the incident channel hourly and post the maintenance window when scheduled.
incident-bot: Incident note: Severity set to HIGH. Incident tracking: INC-2040001111. Oncall handoff recorded: Anna -> Sean.
Anna (oncall): Quick retrospective note — we should add a warmup checklist to the NovaCorp dedicated profile in the console to speed future failovers (kv warm, smoke tests). Natalie, can you draft that?
Natalie P.: Yup. Drafting checklist and will add to the tenant profile in the next 24h.
Lee S.: I'll follow up with the account team to offer an optional post-incident review with NovaCorp next week.
NovaCorp Support: Appreciate the transparency. Please share the RCA once ready.
Anna (oncall): Will do. Closing loop here — handoff complete.
